why: the defective path was entered three times in 5,825 metadata builds, 0.515 per thousand, in this shipped regime
the mechanism in one actionable sentence: at eight streams with prefix caching on a short non-speculative request can land between speculative ones and the unpatched gather then misaligns the gates

the effect on answers was not measured and measuring it was declined: three events in 5,825 builds cannot move a statistic whose noise floor is about thirty times the per-event effect, so the A/B was not run and no claim is made either way

changes.change: two accuracy corrections I had to make to my own C1 text before publishing, after reading each card's actual recipe
detail: MODEL_CARD-K4.md and MODEL_CARD-K5K6-hydrated.md publish their 8,192-token prefix-caching command with NO --speculative-config, and the defect requires speculative tokens (analysis.exact_condition...why[0]: the speculative branch is entered only when spec_sequence_masks is not None). Those two cards therefore state both conditions explicitly: with no MTP the module is a no-op by construction, and at --max-num-seqs 1 no mixed batch can form. An earlier draft of my text had listed fp8 KV and MTP-3 as part of 'this card's flag set', which they are not; the published text attributes them to the measurement arm instead. Only MODEL_CARD-K5K6.md's Recipe B ships --speculative-config mtp/3 together with prefix caching and eight streams.

R2 (and R1/R3) served the context edition's weights, not the card's own checkpoint. All three cards now say so, with the reason it is still the right evidence: the counter reads only the scheduler's host-side arrays, so composition follows the flags and the traffic, and the checkpoint enters only through the size of the KV pool.

changes.change: the opposite statement on the context edition's card: the overlay is NOT recommended for its recipes
changes.not_implied_to_be_unreachable_in_general: the card states that the same instrument entered the path three times in 5,825 builds in the siblings' 8,192-token prefix-caching recipe, that the three cards which ship the cache now recommend the overlay, that the clamp mechanism is bounded rather than proven impossible, and that anyone taking this card's own capped-window prefix-caching option (--max-model-len 256000 with --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align) at more than one sequence is in the regime that fired and should mount the overlay, its rate at that window being unmeasured.

byte_identity_proof: tools/publish_cards.py uploads the local card as README.md, refreshes that repo's DOCS-SHA256SUMS README line, then re-fetches both files from the hub into a throwaway cache under HF_HOME=/var/tmp/hf-home-3 and compares bytes. all_byte_identical is true for the four repos; published_before hashes matched receipts/apc-card-publication.json exactly, so nothing else had moved the cards since the previous pass.
